abstract: Large language models trained on protein sequences learn general coevolutionary relationships at scale, which contain useful structural and functional information. We show that attention maps, matrices of learned pairwise relationships between residues, include information about allostery. This enables prediction of allosteric relationships with no task-specific training, requiring a single input sequence and specified active-site residues, without structural information. Attention maps outperform established structure-based and sequence coevolution-based models across a benchmark of 109 allosteric proteins. In the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, a G-protein coupled receptor, attention maps correlate more strongly with experimental alanine-scanning measurements of allosteric effects on signaling than these comparators. Language model attention also guides efficient, low-throughput experimental discovery of putative allosteric residues in the protease DPP4 and residues coupled to the known allosteric pathway in ACE2. These results enable and demonstrate allosteric relationship prediction in a zero-shot, single-sequence, structure-free manner. We provide this method in the AlloGator web interface.
